name: AntiLife
description: The black/white reversal of Conway's Game of Life.

name: InverseLife
description: A rule by Jason Rampe, showing similar oscillators and gliders to Conway's Game of Life. The black/white reversal of B3678/S23.

name: A strobing rule which makes spearheaders form from chaotic oscillating boundaries.
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: Wickstretcher And The Parasites
description: An explosive strobing rule which forms different wickstretchers of different speeds and sizes, mostly accompanied by a "parasite" or patterns that stick to them and change the size of the wicks.

name: Oils
description: An exploding rule that forms many wickstrechers, along with other patterns such as a c/16 diagonal spaceship.

name: Invertamaze
description: A strobing rule which makes mazes that invert themselves each generation (SEIZURE WARNING).

name: Neon Blobs
description: A strobing rule in which patterns become neon-like explosive patterns.

name: H-trees
description: An exploding rule where H-shaped branches grow from pattern borders.

name: Fuzz
description: An exploding rule in which solid patterns appear.

name: Gnarl
description: A simple exploding rule by Kellie Evans that forms complex patterns from even a single live cell.

name: Snakeskin
description: A rule in which patterns explode and form snake-like patterns.

name: Solid islands grow amongst static
description: A rule in which patterns grow exponentially and form solid patterns inside static-like patterns.

name: Replicator
description: A rule in which every pattern is a replicator.

name: Fredkin
description: A rule in which, like Replicator, every pattern is a replicator. Also known as "Replicator 2".

name: Feux
description: An explosive rule where patterns turn into replicators and flash in and out of existence.

name: Forrest of Ls
description: An explosive rule where the insides of patterns slowy stablize into still formations.

name: Seeds
description: An exploding rule by Brian Silverman in which every cell dies in every generation. It has many simple orthogonal spaceships, though it is in general difficult to create patterns that don't explode.

name: Live Free or Die
description: An exploding rule in which only cells with no neighbors survive. It has many spaceships, puffers, and oscillators, some of infinitely extensible size and period.

name: An exploding rule, one of the few B2 life-like rules that has a replicator.
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: An exploding rule, with still lifes that may form indestructible barriers to growth, which can be used as casing for single-use wires, out of which logic gates can be constructed.
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: Similar to B2/S2345
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: Similar to B2/S2345
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: Serviettes
description: An exploding rule in which every cell dies in every generation (like Seeds). This rule is of interest because of the fabric-like beauty of the patterns that it produces. Also known as "Persian Rug".

name: An exploding rule, it has a one-dimensional asymmetric replicator.
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: Iceballs
description: Small masses of solid living cells flicker in and out of existence. Some reach a critical mass and begin to slowly grow. Also known as "Ice nine".

name: Life without death
description: An expanding rule that produces complex flakes, featuring dense wickstretchers named "ladders". Also known as "Flakes" or "Inkspot".

name: DotLife
description: An exploding rule closely related to Conway's Life. The B-heptomino is a common infinite growth pattern in this rule, though it can be stabilized into a spaceship.

name: Star Trek
description: A rule with several spaceships of various speeds.

name: Flock
description: Patterns tend to quickly settle into dominoes, duoplets and period 2 oscillators. There is a common period 14 shuttle oscillator involving the pre-beehive.

name: Mazectric
description: An expanding rule that crystalizes to form maze-like designs that tend to be straighter (ie. have longer "halls") than the standard maze rule.

name: Maze
description: An expanding rule that crystalizes to form maze-like designs.

name: Magnezones
description: An explosive rule that is liquid with four types of crystals appearing in the liquid.

name: SnowLife
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: Corrosion of Conformity
description: A rule similar to Mazectric but without S3. A slow burn from almost any starting pattern, resulting in a rusting away of the local continuum.

name: EightFlock
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: LowLife
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: This rule has 6 small still lifes, the tub, the hive, the aircraft carrier, the loaf, the mango, and the pond. However, there are no still lifes with more than 8 and less than 20 cells. There are also a few common oscillators, including the blinker and the toad, and lots of rare ones.
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: Conway's Life
description: A chaotic rule that is by far the most well-known and well-studied. It exhibits highly complex behavior.

name: EightLife
description: Also known as "Pulsar Life".

name: Shoots and Roots
description: Shoots are slow growing, well-ordered patterns, while Roots grow faster than shoots, and explosive as they grow.

name: Lifeguard 2
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: Coral
description: An exploding rule in which patterns grow slowly and form coral-like textures.

name: 3-4 Life
description: An exploding rule that was initially thought to be a stable alternative to Conway's Life, until computer simulation found that most patterns tend to explode. It has many small oscillators and simple period 3 orthogonal and diagonal spaceships.

name: Dance
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: Bacteria
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: Never happy
description: An explosive rule where patterns slowly form diamond-like shapes and slowly explode.

name: Blinkers
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: Assimilation
description: A very stable rule that forms permanent diamond-shaped patterns with partially filled interiors. Like in 2×2, patterns made of blocks will permanently remain made of blocks.

name: Long Life
description: A stable rule that gets its name from the fact that it has many simple extremely high period oscillators.

name: Spiral and polygonal growth
description: A rule with "plow" structures that move along an edge of a polygon, increasing its size (turning corners and thickening it as they go), corner-extenders that create these in their wake, and nontrivial interactions based on these (such as a 16-cell methuselah that takes 12127116559 generations to become a period-2 oscillator)

name: Gems
description: An exploding rule with many smaller high-period oscillators and a c/5648 spaceship.

name: Gems Minor
description: An exploding rule with many smaller high-period oscillators and a c/2068 spaceship.

name: Grounded Life
description: A stable rule "one outer-totalistic condition away from Life", where neither of the standard spaceships works, and the most common spaceship is an orthogonal 2c/5 spaceship called "Glider 3736".

name: Land Rush
description: Expanding chaos organizing itself into plowed fields.

name: Eppstein
description: An exploding rule explored by Dean Hickerson and David Eppstein.

name: Bugs
description: An explosive rule with many high density spaceships.

name: Cheerios
description: An explosive rule where patterns explode while "cheerios" form in the chaotic mess.

name: Holstein
description: A self-complementary rule. Black regions are surrounded by froth and tend to eventually collapse starting from the corners, but can be stabilized in various ways by oscillators on their boundaries. c/3, c/4, c/5 and c/7 orthogonal spaceships are known.

name: Diamoeba
description: A chaotic pattern that forms large diamonds with chaotically oscillating boundaries. Known to have quadratically-growing patterns. Like in 2×2, patterns made of blocks will permanently remain made of blocks.

name: Amoeba
description: A chaotic rule that is well balanced between life and death; it forms patterns with chaotic interiors and wildly moving boundaries.

name: Pseudo Life
description: A chaotic rule with evolution that resembles Conway's Life, but few patterns from Life work in this rule because the glider is unstable.

name: Geology
description: A very well-balanced and chaotic rule that forms large "continents" of live cells surrounded by chaos at a roughly 50% density, but they eventually erode away into smaller "islands". It is symmetric under on-off reversal.

name: HighFlock
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)
A chaotic rule with many simple still lifes, oscillators and spaceships. Its name comes from the fact that it sends patterns made up of 2 × 2 blocks to patterns made up of 2 × 2 blocks.

name: IronFlock
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: HighLife
description: A chaotic rule very similar to Conway's Life that is of interest because it has a simple replicator.

name: Land Rush 2
description: An exploding rule that got confused with Land Rush, likely due to a typo.  It does contain a period 4 orthogonal c/2 ship.

name: Virus
description: An exploding rule where the T-tetromino is a blinker puffer, appropriate because it evolves into traffic light in Life, also made of blinkers.

name: IronLife
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: sqrt replicator rule
description: Name comes from a dirty orthogonal replicator, formerly known as the logarithmic replicator rule.

name: Slow Blob
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: DrighLife
description: A mix between DryLife and HighLife
(LifeWiki gives no description)

name: Castles
description: A rule where patterns almost explode into castle-like stable patterns.

name: Black/white reversal of InverseLife.
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: Stains
description: A stable rule in which most patterns tend to "fill in" bounded regions. Most nearby rules (such as coagulations) tend to explode.

name: Day & Night
description: A stable rule that is symmetric under on-off reversal. Many patterns exhibiting highly complex behavior have been found for it.

name: LowDeath without Death
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: An exploding 2x2-like rule with a small 4c/13o replicator, of which guns and W110 unit cells had been constructed
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: LowFlockDeath
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: Life SkyHigh
description: A rule that is similar to HighLife but adds a B8 and S6 to the rulestring, hence, the name "SkyHigh".

name: LowDeath
description: HighLife's replicator works in this rule, albeit with a different evolution sequence due to the result of B38/S23's "pedestrian" effect.

name: Morley
description: A rule in which random patterns tend to stabilize extremely quickly. Has a very common slow-moving spaceship and slow-moving puffer. Also known as "Move".

name: DryLife without Death
description: Similar to Life without death, but patterns tend to grow quadratically instead of forming 'ladders'.

name: DryFlock
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: Mazectric with Mice
description: Some "mice" run back and forth in the halls of the maze.

name: Maze with Mice
description: Similar to B37/S1234, some "mice" run back and forth in the continually-stretching halls of the maze.

name: DryLife
description: An exploding rule closely related to Conway's Life, named after the fact that standard spaceships bigger than the glider do not function in the rule. Has a small 9c/28 orthogonal puffer based on the R-pentomino, which resembles the switch engine in the possibility of combining several to form a spaceship.

name: Plow World
description: An explosive rule, some of the patterns can turn into wickstretchers.

name: Coagulations
description: An exploding rule in which patterns tend to expand forever, producing a thick "goo" as it does so. Surprisingly, Coagulations actually has one less birth condition than Stains.

name: Pedestrian Life without Death
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: Pedestrian Flock
description: A mix between Pedestrian Life and Flock.

name: HoneyFlock
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: Pedestrian Life
description: A close Life variant with a number of distinctive natural growth patterns and (5,2)c/190 oblique spaceships.

name: HoneyLife
description: A mix between Pedestrian Life and EightLife.

name: Electrified Maze
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: Oscillators Rule
description: Random patterns shrink to tiny oscillators, with periods anywhere between 1 ("still lifes") and 16. Larger periods are rare.

name: Walled cities
description: A stable rule by David Macfarlane that forms centers of pseudo-random activity separated by walls.

name: Majority
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: Vote 4/5
description: A modification of the standard Gérard Vichniac voting rule, also known as "Anneal", used as a model for majority voting.

name: Lifeguard 1
description: (LifeWiki gives no description)

name: Rings 'n' Slugs
description: A rule in which patterns stabilize into "Rings" and "Slugs".

name: Vote
description: Standard Gérard Vichniac voting rule, also known as "Majority", used as a model for majority voting.

name: 9:43 at Knight
description: Stable; by EricG.

name: Banners
description: Exploding; by Mirek Wójtowicz. A rule that often produces spaceships with growing fluttering banners.

name: BelZhab
description: Exploding; by ?. A rule exhibiting Zhabotinsky reactions.

name: BelZhab Sediment
description: Exploding; by Jason Rampe. The rule creates BelZhab-like patterns that have growing regions of "sedimentary deposits".

name: Bloomerang
description: Expanding; by John Elliott (July 2000). A wave rule that rebounds into a kinder, gentler form of kaleidoscopics — rounded, soft, full, and slow.

name: Bombers
description: Chaotic; by Mirek Wójtowicz. A close variant of the Star Wars rule with many more history steps, resulting in beautiful ships, puffers and oscillators.

name: Brain 6
description: Chaotic; by Michael Sweney. An interesting variation of the immortal Brian's Brain, with many patterns constructed.

name: Brian's Brain
description: Chaotic; by Brian Silverman. Also called BB, or simply Brain, this is unquestionably one of the best known and most beautiful CA rules. If we name the possible cell values based on a simplistic neural analogy, viz. 0 = "ready", 1 = "firing", 2 = "refractory", then this simple rule can be stated thusly: Only a cell in the ready state may fire and it will only do so if exactly 2 of its neighbors are firing. After firing for one step, a cell spends a step in the refractory state before regaining readiness. Although the rule is relatively old, it has never been systematically explored. The rule is

name: Burst
description: Chaotic; by Michael Sweney. A rule related to Nova, Prairie Fire and others which features large areas of cells that slowly die out or decay into oscillators. Named after a characteristic exploding oscillator. Similar to Day & Night in that constructions can be built both with inside and outside oscillations and growth/decay. Has still lifes similar to Conway Life. [LifeWiki B/S/C column reads 'B3468/0235678/C9' (typo); normalised from S/B/C column '0235678/3468/9']

name: Burst II
description: Chaotic; by Michael Sweney. This rule is basically Burst without the single cell still life. It supports slow and fast spaceships, oscillators, and methuselahs as well as a very characteristic p500+ oscillator.

name: Caterpillars
description: Chaotic; by Mirek Wójtowicz. Named after its very common caterpillar-like patterns.

name: Chenille
description: Exploding; by ?.  [LifeWiki B/S/C column reads 'B24567/05678/C6' (typo); normalised from S/B/C column '05678/24567/6']

name: Circuit Genesis
description: Expanding; by Charles A. Rockafellor. Circuitry which evolves far beyond its programming and continues to do so long after the initial intput have taken the borders elsewhere.

name: Cooties
description: Exploding; by Rudy Rucker. A very vivacious rule, with cells crawling around like mad lice.

name: Ebb and Flow
description: Exploding; by Michael Sweney. A slow exploding rule with interesting internal dynamics within the growth boundaries. Different types of symmetries will often determine whether a pattern grows indefinitely or dies out. Presents challenging engineering problems. Best viewed in MCell with the standard color palette at speeds of 10 or slower.

name: Ebb and Flow II
description: Exploding; by Michael Sweney. A close variant of Ebb and Flow that supports simple gliders.

name: Faders
description: Exploding; by Rudy Rucker and John Walker. A "genetic" cross of Life and Brian's Brain. A dead Faders cell requires exactly 2 firing neighbors to get turned on. A firing Faders cell keeps firing if it has exactly 2 firing neighbors. And when a Faders cell leaves the firing state it goes into a sequence of refractory states.

name: Fireworks
description: Exploding; by John Elliott. Nearly perfect fireworks simulation. It produces interesting results from both random and prepared initial states. Even several cells scattered over the lattice will produce long-running ravishing pictures.

name: Flaming Starbows
description: Exploding; by Charles A. Rockafellor. In this world beautiful expanding diamonds and oddly off-parallelograms sweep across the screen leaving trails of fire and spirals of autogenesis. Reminiscent of a mutant spawn of Faders and mad Zhabotinsky spirals.

name: Frogs
description: Chaotic; by Scott Robert Ladd. A rule named after its very common frog-like gliders.

name: Frozen Spirals
description: Cyclic; by Mirek Wójtowicz. This rule features a popular Zhabotinsky reaction, but with one difference — spirals have icicles in their vertices.

name: Glisserati
description: Exploding; by John Elliott (May 2000). "From simple seeds this rule is often highly glideriferous, generating striking kaleidoscopic patterns. Sometimes, though, as in the Glidathon orbit, it is more sparse, in the vein of rules such as Transers, but with much longer transients, providing an uncanny sense of "perpetual motion". Since I found this rule I've become aware of other recently discovered kaleidoscopic glider rules, such as Snake and TransersII, which share many of the same objects, though I've yet to see a Glidathon style orbit in them (which doesn't mean they aren't there - no one's

name: Glissergy
description: Exploding; by John Elliott (May 2000). "This rule differs from Glisserati only in its cellsize (5 rather than 7). As would be expected, this change is an activity booster - so much so, that, unlike Glisserati, this rule has long transients from random as well as simple starts. Think of it as the pin-iferous answer to Brian's Brain." — John Elliott [LifeWiki B/S/C column reads 'B245678/035678/C5' (typo); normalised from S/B/C column '035678/245678/5']

name: Lava
description: Expanding; by Mirek Wójtowicz. All patterns are getting very slowly filled with hot lava.

name: Lines
description: Stable; by Anders Starmark (September 2000). This rule quickly self-organizes into linear structures, with separate orthogonally hatched areas. To see the most interesting behaviour, seed the universe with a circle with r≥40 and a density of 20%.

name: Living On The Edge
description: Chaotic; by Mirek Wójtowicz (February 2000). Also known as LOTE. In this very chaotic rule, it is hard to tell if patterns will survive or die out.

name: Meteor Guns
description: Expanding; by Charles A. Rockafellor. Almost any design above a certain level of complexity results in a slowly exploding ball of fire which then spits fairly large numbers of generational gliders, the titular "meteors". There are easily discovered stable oscillators and static patterns. A truly satisfying environment (if only finding a limited growth meteor gun were as easy...).

name: Nova
description: Expanding; by Mirek Wójtowicz. Very lovely rule characterized by vibrant yet stately streaming growth from solid seeds. The growth patterns and active border have a fascinating geometry, the particulars of which are sensitive to the size and shape of the initial solid.

name: OrthoGo
description: Exploding; by John Elliott (December 1999). This simple rule supports spontaneous orthogonally productive "glider colliders". But otherwise it seems fairly quiescent.

name: Prairie on fire
description: Exploding; by Mirek Wójtowicz. This rule covers the lattice with fire. For best results use yellow-red cells color settings.

name: RainZha
description: Exploding; by Rudy Rucker and John Walker. The simplest "Zhabotinsky" style cellular automaton. It spontaneously generates spirals from an initial random pattern.

name: Rake
description: Exploding; by Brian Prentice. This rule is a simple variation of the Worms rule and is characterized by the numerous rake puffers that it generates. Together with the puffers, it generates many ships and expanding wings. These elements can easily be arranged to collide and form ships and puffers of arbitrary complexity.

name: SediMental
description: Exploding; by John Elliott. From a random seed state of 30% ones, the rule tends to form stable "islands", with active coastlines and fascinating inter-island "commerce". But an orbit's fate is quite sensitive to the starting percentage. Below 25% or so the world remains sparsely Brain-like, whereas somewhere above 30% the islands begin to accrete into larger "landmasses", so that by 40% you nearly always end up with a single huge "continent". As for simple seeds, they often lead to surprising results. And the rule clearly has great potential from the "engineering" standpoint.

name: Snake
description: Exploding; by Brian Prentice. This rule is a simple variation of the Worms rule. It contains two interesting oscillators, a 3*3 square and a shuttle, among its basic elements. By combining copies of the square, many beautiful oscillators can be generated. The rule also generates many puffers one of which generates a sequence of shuttles. The tail generated by the shuttle puffer resembles a snake.

name: Soft Freeze
description: Chaotic; by John Elliott. "The rule is delicately poised between "solid" and "liquid" phases. From many simple seeds it forms "living crystals" - the crystals form, melt, and reform seemingly indefinitely, in balance with an active phase. The areas of melting can shrink to a point where you're sure everything will freeze over, and then they stage a comeback. From random starts, this rule resembles a nice poised rule from Wójtowicz called "Living on the Edge", only this one is even more "on the edge". (BTW, though the rule definition looks as though I took LOTE as a starting point, I actually c

name: Spirals
description: Exploding; by ?. The rule produces beautiful stable spirals that unroll forever.

name: Star Wars
description: Exploding; by Mirek Wójtowicz (March 1999). Also known as MirekGro, this is a very interesting and beautiful rule producing deep space battle scenes; a paradise for patterns' creators in the tradition of Conway Life. It's a successful combination of famous Brian's Brain with a stabilizing factor. "StarWars is also an interesting rule from the low-investment standpoint. In particular, it is notable for the abundance, intricacy, and variety of its naturally-occurring glider guns. In general when running "au naturel" StarWars is active to a degree almost reminiscent of Brain, with the distinction

name: Sticks
description: Exploding; by Rudy Rucker. This interesting rule builds a variety of sticks, with ships floating among them.

name: Swirl
description: Chaotic; by Scott Robert Ladd. While spirals are common in CAs (see for example RainZha or Cyclic CAs), Swirl's whirlers are of the rarer discrete variety - isolated "whirlpools" in an otherwise dead sea. There are two sizes of whirlpools that occur regularly. Ladd calls the smaller the "swirlpool" and the larger the "flamewhirl". Also there is a glider with a flickering double tail which Ladd aptly refers to as a fire or flame glider.

name: Thrill Grill
description: Expanding; by John Elliott (July 2000). Sparkling dynamics inhabit and rearrange a grill-like background of one-cells.

name: Transers
description: Exploding; by John Elliott. A beautiful and dynamic rule with many distinctive entities that occur "in the wild", with remarkable inter-entity transformations.

name: Transers II
description: Exploding; by Michael Sweney.

name: Wanderers
description: Exploding; by Mirek Wójtowicz. A rule very similar to "Prairie on fire", but creates interesting dynamically moving patterns.

name: Worms
description: Exploding; by Mirek Wójtowicz. A very vigorous rule producing crowds of disgusting worms.

name: Xtasy
description: Exploding; by John Elliott (July 2000). From simple seeds in a closed universe this is a lovely kaleidoscopic wave rule that tends to do extended meditations on the letter X.

name: Gnarl (LtL)
description: exploding rule by Kellie Evans; equals B1/S0V

name: Majority (LtL)
description: stable rule by David Griffeath; MCell form R4,C0,M1,S41..81,B41..81,NM (HROT excludes middle cell, MCell M1 includes it)

name: Bosco's Rule
description: chaotic rule by Kellie Evans, known for hollow 'bugs' spaceships; MCell form R5,C0,M1,S34..58,B34..45,NM

name: Waffle
description: expanding rule by Kellie Evans

name: Majorly
description: expanding rule by David Griffeath

name: Globe
description: expanding rule by Mirek Wojtowicz

name: Bugsmovie
description: chaotic rule by David Griffeath (MCell 'Bugs'); name on page is Bugsmovie

name: ModernArt
description: chaotic rule by Charles A. Rockafellor; 255 states

name: Marine
description: chaotic rule by MathAndCode; custom neighbourhood N@03ddef (HROT, not plain LtL)

name: Factorio
description: semistable rule by H. H. P. M. P. Cole; cross neighbourhood (N+), HROT not plain LtL

name: Coexistence
description: chaotic rule by bubblegum; weighted neighbourhood, HROT only

name: Hash
description: chaotic rule by b-engine; HROT hash neighbourhood

name: Hexagonal Life
description: Name appears only as a forum thread title '(Hexagonal Life)' linked from the hexagonal neighbourhood page; the page uses B2/S34H as its notation example

name: Gnarl (von Neumann)
description: LifeWiki Gnarl disambiguation: 'the von Neumann neighbourhood rule B1/S0V' (Hensel B1e2ak3inqy4ny5e/S01c2cn3c4c)
